title: Unified stability matrix and rollback playbook for serving and console
creator: Jordan Patel
description:
Goal: produce an actionable LTS support matrix and rollout/rollback playbook spanning Runtime, Redwood API, SDKs, and Console. Deliverables: (1) canonical matrix mapping releases to stability lanes, supported client versions, and compatibility guarantees; (2) automated pre-release gate checks and upgrade validators; (3) rollback/mitigation runbook and a small demo of upgrade tooling that performs compatibility checks against pinned customer fleets.

Rationale: Customers require predictable upgrade windows and a clear SLO for backward compatibility. Current gaps: lack of machine-checkable compatibility assertions, limited console guidance during canaries, and inconsistent SDK pinning behavior that leads to runtime errors during server-client mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Published LTS matrix artifact in Confluence with per-surface rows: runtime, api, sdk, console, and per-release columns; 2) Two new pre-release validators merged (api-schema-check, kvcache-schema-compat) that run in CI and gate release branches; 3) Canary rollout steps documented in console UI prototype and validated with synthetic traffic against dedicated test fleet; 4) Rollback runbook validated in an internal dry-run and stored in runbooks/playbooks/rollback-lts.md; 5) Postmortem template and dashboard links included.
notes:
Early design decisions: prefer semantic-major+compatibility-label approach instead of strict semver enforcement because runtime ABI changes can be orthogonal to API semantics. We will represent compatibility as a tri-state tag: compatible, compatible-with-shims, incompatible.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Strict semver + auto-block on major bump: simpler but blocks necessary performance-only ABI changes.
- Compatibility tag + validators: allows faster iterations but requires robust validators and clear customer-facing messaging.

Current plan: implement compatibility validators and an automated compatibility-report that surfaces in the console during releases.
decisions: 1) Use tri-state compatibility tags (compatible / compatible-with-shims / incompatible) across surfaces. 2) Gate releases with two CI validators initially (schema and kvcache), expand to runtime kernel fingerprinting later. 3) Console will surface compatibility warnings and block one-click upgrades if validators fail. 4) SDKs must include runtime-compat metadata in package manifest by runtime-2.4.
